sample_unit: coronary angiography studies (development set; also 2247 UCSF external studies, 82 prospective STEMI cases, 200 human-evaluation cases)

links.outcome: Clinician and student accuracy identifying reduced RVSF with versus without AI assistance
links.effect: AI assistance improved accuracy for cardiologists (72.1-77.6%) and medical students (43.5-64.0%); AI alone reached 79.5% accuracy; cardiologists with AI had highest specificity (84.6%).
links.quote: In a human performance evaluation (n = 200), artificial intelligence (AI) assistance improved accuracy of identifying RVSF for cardiologists (72.1-77.6%) and medical students (43.5-64.0%).

links.outcome: Model discrimination on external site versus internal test set
links.effect: AUROC 0.80 (95% CI 0.76-0.84) internally versus 0.75 (95% CI 0.72-0.77) at UCSF (n=2247 studies; 30% reduced RVSF vs 10.5%); modest drop with different prevalence.
links.quote: External validation demonstrated AUROC 0.75 (95% CI: 0.72-0.77) on the UCSF dataset (n = 2247 studies; 30% reduced RVSF).

screen.reason: The study develops, prospectively deploys, and tests an AI tool (DeepRV) for coronary angiogram analysis, and evaluates clinician performance with versus without AI assistance in a reader study.
